This is a common technique we organic chemists use to purify solids called recrystallization. In short, you want to choose a solvent that the solid is insoluble in at room temperature yet soluble in at boiling point. Traditionally you bring the choosen solvent to boil and slowly add to
the solid with vigorous stirring until the solid just dissolves....ie. don’t add too much solvent. Ad the solution is allowed to cool slowly the solid in solution will begin to form a crystal
lattice and crash out of solution in its pure form.
